title: Pareto-Grid-Guided Large Language Models for Fast and High-Quality Heuristics Design in Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

publication.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-based heuristic design for multi-objective combinatorial optimization
mechanism.populationDetail: The heuristic population is an undivided set; Algorithm 3 appends offspring to the accumulated population and filters to a non-dominated final output, although Section 4.5 describes non-dominated PFG representatives as the next generation.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Each iteration derives a reusable elite set from non-dominated representatives in occupied PFG objective cells; it is multi-elite but not a separate persistent archive or behavior-descriptor QD archive.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Algorithm 3 recomputes PFG elites from the accumulated population each iteration and appends offspring until final non-dominated filtering; Section 4.5 instead describes the elite representatives as the next generation, so population pruning is inconsistently specified.
mechanism.generationDetail: Mutation broadly modifies one selected heuristic, while crossover uses two heuristics from different semantic clusters as true parents and synthesizes a new algorithm, optionally guided by reflection.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The objective vector (average negative hypervolume and runtime) is the primary fitness signal, not auxiliary metadata. Reflection suggestions are generated from parent implementations rather than returned by the evaluator.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The local pool is a randomly sampled PFG cell plus neighboring cells; mutation samples one heuristic from a cluster, while crossover samples a second from another cluster. The alternative global branch samples two from E(t). No additional inspiration/reference set is retrieved.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: LLM semantic clustering of objective-selected heuristics explicitly controls within-cluster mutation versus cross-cluster parent mating; this combined PFG-plus-semantic mating policy is not directly represented by a current dedicated taxonomy category.

provenance.citationWarning: Coverage gaps: the survey currently omits MPaGE from flat multi-individual populations, multi-elite archives, incremental insertion, prompt structures, model static assignment, state-independent exploration-exploitation control, and parent-selection discussion. Do not label the objective-grid PFG as a behavior-descriptor QD archive; it is a derived elite parent pool. Parent count varies by mutation/crossover path. Population update is inconsistent between Section 4.5 and Algorithm 3; this draft follows the pseudocode and flags the ambiguity.
